statement: No agreement between the two leading compute jurisdictions sets verifiable limits on training compute or capabilities (Official readouts, treaty texts; by 2028-06-30)
status_at_phase_end: Holding (toward YES) at end-2023: Bloc A and Bloc B both endorsed a non-binding multilateral declaration on frontier-AI risk and, at a leaders' summit, agreed to hold government talks on AI risk and safety; neither set any verifiable compute or capability limit.

items.summary: 28 countries plus a regional union, including both Bloc A and Bloc B, endorsed a declaration recognising frontier-AI risks (including potential catastrophic harm) and resolving to cooperate on risk understanding; it contains no limits or verification.
items.detail: Bloc G government, 'Countries agree to safe and responsible development of frontier AI in landmark Bletchley Declaration', 2023-11-01, and the declaration text (both verified via web_extract this run; the declaration page shows a later 'updated 13 February 2025' stamp, only the 2023 text is used). Signatories include the Bloc A and Bloc B.

items.summary: Leaders of Bloc A and Bloc B met and 'affirmed the need to address the risks of advanced AI systems and improve AI safety' through bilateral government talks; no limits on compute or capabilities were agreed.
items.detail: White House readout of President Biden's meeting with President Xi Jinping, Woodside, California, 2023-11-15 (archived page verified via web_extract this run).

items.summary: At the same summit, a plan for state-led pre-release testing of frontier models was agreed by 11 governments and 10 developers; Bloc B was not among the governments listed, so it is not a bilateral limit-setting arrangement.
items.detail: Bloc G government, 'Safety Testing: Chair's Statement of Session Outcomes, 2 November 2023' (verified via web_extract this run).
